Subject: Renewal planning — capacity + term options

Sean —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Our renewal with Redwood comes up at the end of August and we need to lock in an approach that lets us: (1) annualize some of the spend, (2) preserve a modest burst lane for spikes tied to product launches, and (3) avoid a hard overage exposure for Q4 ramp.

Current thinking from our side (very high level):
- Explore a 24–36 month option with a step-up ramp in year 2
- Keep a deferred burst bucket that we can draw from for launches (we'd like predictable pricing for that)
- Request an auto-renew window with an opt-out notice of 60 days for enterprise procurement

Can you send a proposal template or an approach you usually use for this (structure, crediting, billing cadence)? I've attached our month-by-month token usage for the last 12 months. Procurement is looped in on the cc.

Best,
Elisa Gomez
Head of Platform Ops
Acme Data

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jul 2028 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity + term options

Elisa — thanks for the data and the clear asks. High-level approach below; I attached a short proposal sketch (PDF) with the numbers redacted until we align on structure.

Proposal concept (summary):
1) Anchored multi-year: 24 months by default with an option to extend to 36 months at a pre-agreed uplift. Anchor year 1 to the current effective run-rate (protects you from front-loading large prepayments).
2) Deferred burst pool: purchase a dedicated burst bucket sized for 2–3 large releases per year. Bursts draw down from the pool at a discounted overage rate; unused burst credits carry forward for 4 quarters.
3) Canary smoothing: for the first 3 months post-sign, we provide a soft canary allowance where spikes up to 150% of baseline are smoothed and not charged against escalator triggers.
4) Auto-renew: 60-day notice for contract opt-out (enterprise default), with a negotiated true-up window once per year.

Next steps I propose:
- If this structure sounds reasonable, I'll create a priced term sheet and route to Finance/Legal for a fallback credit clause (we call it the "fiscal fallback") — a small, pre-agreed credit band if usage wildly exceeds the projected ramp in months 2–6.
- Camila (SE) will confirm technical sizing for the burst pool so we price correctly.

Attachments: Redwood_Proposal_anchored-deferred-burst.pdf (proposal sketch)

Happy to hop on a 30 min call w/ procurement to walk through the trade-offs.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Elisa — appreciate the fast alignment on structure during today's call. Per our conversation, here's the agreed framework to put into the term sheet:

1) Term: 24 months anchored to current run-rate; optional extension to 36 months at a pre-negotiated uplift (customer opt-in at month 18).
2) Billing cadence: annualized billing with a quarterly true-up (this was Acme's preference).
3) Deferred burst: a 3-release burst pool sized per Camila's attachment (linked). Unused burst credits roll forward for 4 quarters.
4) Canary smoothing: months 1–3 post-sign will have a smoothing window (spikes up to 150% baseline not to trigger escalators).
5) Fiscal fallback: Redwood agrees to a limited credit band equal to 1% of committed value if months 2–6 usage exceeds the projected ramp by >200% (Finance approved this on the condition that the burst pool sizing is validated).
6) Auto-renew: 60-day opt-out notice; one yearly true-up window.
